correlates.name: Pleural Effusion / Intrapleural Edema
correlates.presentation: the lecturer frames it as edema of the intrapleural space, which compresses lung and impairs expansion.
correlates.pathophysiology: lymphatic drainage of the intrapleural space fails while hydrostatic filtration continues, so fluid accumulates far beyond the normal 10 mL.

correlates.name: Pneumothorax
correlates.pathophysiology: the parietal pleura is punctured, so the intrapleural space equilibrates with atmosphere and its pressure becomes 0.

correlates.name: Emphysema
correlates.presentation: less inspiratory muscle force is needed to inflate; the problem is emptying the lung. FRC is elevated, accessory muscle use and a barrel chest follow (Slide 5).
correlates.pathophysiology: inflammation drives enzymatic destruction of elastin, partially destroying the lung's elastic properties. Compliance rises, elastic recoil falls.
correlates.treatment: pursed-lip breathing - slower expiration against partly closed lips raises airway pressure enough to keep large airways open (Slide 22).

correlates.name: Pulmonary Fibrosis
correlates.presentation: progressive dyspnea and a dry, hacking cough. The lecture's board vignette is a 64-year-old retired sandblaster whose HRCT shows diffuse interstitial thickening and scarring (Slide 23).
correlates.pathophysiology: additional collagen fibers inserted into the parenchyma make the lung less compliant and more elastic, so a much more negative intrapleural pressure is needed to achieve a normal tidal volume.

correlates.name: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome
correlates.presentation: the lecture's radiograph shows a normally aerated right lung and a completely opaque, collapsed left lung (Slide 16).
correlates.pathophysiology: mostly premature infants born with insufficient surfactant; Laplace collapsing forces go unopposed and alveoli close.
correlates.treatment: antenatal steroid injections to the mother aid lung maturation and surfactant production. Otherwise nasal continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP) applies positive pressure to hold the alveoli open; no surgery is required.

correlates.name: Asthma
correlates.pathophysiology: airway narrowing from pro-inflammatory mediators - histamine and leukotrienes - plus parasympathetic muscarinic tone. Because resistance scales with r^4, a small diameter change has an outsized effect.
correlates.treatment: beta-receptor agonists (isoproterenol, albuterol) reproduce sympathetic dilation; muscarinic antagonists (atropine) block the constricting arm, with the cardiac caution above.

formulas.name: Lung Compliance
formulas.equation: Compliance = change in volume per unit change in pressure; elastance is its inverse
formulas.meaning: Emphysema destroys elastic fibers so compliance rises and recoil falls — inspiration is easy, expiration is hard; fibrosis lays down extra fibers so compliance falls and recoil rises — inspiration is hard, expiration is easy
formulas.normalValue: FRC is higher than normal in emphysema and lower than normal in fibrosis

formulas.name: Transmural Pressure
formulas.equation: Transmural = pressure inside a compartment - pressure outside it
formulas.meaning: At every stage of the breathing cycle transmural pressure is positive and directed outward, and that is what holds the lung open — not the sign of the intrapleural pressure by itself
formulas.normalValue: +5 at rest, +5.5 during inspiration, +8 at peak inspiration, +7.5 during expiration

formulas.name: Dynamic Airway Collapse in Emphysema
formulas.equation: Large airway transmural pressure = airway pressure - intrapleural pressure
formulas.meaning: Normally the large airway sits at +25 against an intrapleural +20, giving a +5 that keeps it open; in emphysema the airway pressure falls to +15 against the same +20, so transmural pressure turns negative and the airway collapses on expiration
formulas.normalValue: This is why emphysema patients purse their lips — it raises airway pressure and keeps transmural pressure positive

formulas.name: Intrapleural Fluid Balance
formulas.equation: Hydrostatic -5 inward, oncotic +5 outward, with the oncotic forces cancelling
formulas.meaning: About 10 mL of pleural fluid provides cohesion and lubrication, drained by lymphatics — when that drainage fails the result is a pleural effusion
formulas.normalValue: Atmospheric 760 mmHg against intrapleural 756 mmHg, a 4 mmHg difference at rest
